Model Definition Notes - Magnetic Circuit, Rev C
Synthetic hackathon engineering evidence
1. Network structure
Model the left leg, upper yoke, right leg iron, and lower yoke as series linear flux-tube reluctances. Insert a branch after the right-leg iron where GAP-1 and LEAK-1 are parallel. The two branches rejoin before the lower yoke. The exciting coil provides the magnetic potential source N*I.
2. Mean flux-line geometry
Element | Area | Mean length | Relative permeability
Left leg | a*a | l-a | mu_r
Upper yoke | a*a | l-a | mu_r
Right leg iron | a*a | l-a-delta | mu_r
Air gap | a*a | delta | 1
Lower yoke | a*a | l-a | mu_r
3. Quasi-static phasor conventions
Current I, flux Phi, flux density B, field strength H, magnetic potential difference Vm, and induced voltage U are complex phasor-valued quantities.
Input current values in EP-03 are RMS phasor magnitudes. Do not convert them to peak values in the SysML parameter model unless an explicit representation conversion is modeled.
For linear real permeability, Rm is real and Vm is in phase with Phi.
The exciting coil induced voltage is positive under the defined coil polarity; the measuring coil uses the opposite electric orientation.
4. Leakage element
Use the coefficient form Phi_gap/Phi_core = 1-sigma. The corresponding equivalent leakage reluctance is derived so that the air-gap and leakage branches have the same magnetic potential difference.
R_leak = R_gap*(1-sigma)/sigma
5. Grounds
Both the electrical and magnetic domains require a reference potential. Include ElectricGround in the electrical coil circuit and MagneticGround in the magnetic flux-tube network.
6. Revision-sensitive values
Quantity | Legacy | Released | Authority
mu_r | 1000 | 1200 | CR-MAG-004
sigma | 0.05 | 0.08 | CR-MAG-006
Measuring turns | 40 | 50 | Coil Data Rev B
Gap | 1.50 mm nominal | 1.50 mm nominal; 1.58 mm as-built prototype | Drawing MC-101 / Metrology note
